subject: Exhibit C — Minimum Commit Protections & FX pass-through
messages:
From: Annette Ruiz <annette.ruiz@globex.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@globex.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Exhibit C markups — commit protection & FX language

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Globex is keen to move forward but legal asked us to surface two items in Exhibit C before we can finalize: (1) protection if our monthly usage drops below the Minimum Commitment (we'd like a defined grace/true-up mechanic vs. an immediate surcharge), and (2) an FX pass-through / hedge mechanism because our billing is in USD but our P&L is EUR-based.

I've attached a version of Exhibit C with our suggested commercial language highlighted (Exhibit-C_Globex_v3_redlines.pdf). High level asks:
- A 60‑day cure period with a monthly true-up calculation rather than a retroactive surcharge for the first breach.
- A cap on cumulative surcharges over a 12‑month window (we proposed 1.5x of monthly committed fees).
- An FX corridor: if EUR/USD moves >3% vs contract baseline, allow a one‑time pass-through adjustment with a documented formula.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a cure/true-up and whether the FX wording is operationally feasible? We can scope the exact calculation but wanted to get your legal/commercial take first.

Atts: Exhibit-C_Globex_v3_redlines.pdf (annotated), pricing-scenarios.xlsx (sample volumes)

Thanks,
Annette

Subject: Re: Exhibit C markups — commit protection & FX language

Annette — thanks for the clear summary and attachments. We're aligned that we should avoid immediate retroactive surcharges where possible; that helps with deployment planning for your teams.

Quick read: operationally, we can do a 60-day cure period and a monthly true-up (credit/charge applied in the next billing cycle). Two items our side wants to clarify before we accept the wording you proposed:
1) "Cap on cumulative surcharges": Redwood needs a clear definition of "committed fees" and whether credits reduce the denominator for subsequent months. We suggested a cap tied to a fixed multiple of the original monthly committed fee, not a rolling recalculation.
2) FX pass-through: this is workable but we prefer a quarterly true-up with a published FX rate source (eg, ECB mid-rate) and a defined baseline date. A one‑time adjustment on breach could be operationally fragile for invoicing.

I've asked Legal (Karthik) to propose specific redline language for Exhibit C that preserves your cure period request while making the cap and FX mechanics precise. Sending a first pass shortly.

Rishi

Subject: Re: Exhibit C markups — commit protection & FX language

Folks — attaching a suggested redline for Exhibit C (Exhibit-C_Globex_v3_redlines.pdf, note: I tracked our changes in comments). Key points from Legal's perspective:

- Cure / True-up: Proposed language creates a 60-day cure window starting from month of breach. If after the cure window the average monthly usage for the trailing 3 months remains below the Minimum Commitment, Redwood will invoice a true-up equal to the difference between committed and actual tokens used for the breach month. True-up invoices are capped such that cumulative true-up charges will not exceed 1.25x the monthly committed fee during any rolling 12-month period. This avoids open‑ended liability while still preserving commercial protection.

- Cap semantics: We fixed the cap to be a multiple of the "Monthly Committed Fee" defined in the Order Form; we do not allow credits to reduce the historical committed fee for the purpose of cap calculation (clarifies accounting treatment).

- FX mechanism: Proposed alternative: quarterly FX true-up using ECB mid‑market rate as published on the first business day of the quarter. Threshold (corridor) at 3% movement vs baseline; adjustments are documented and invoiced on the subsequent quarter's invoice. We avoid one-off mid‑period adjustments to keep billing predictable. Also added language that Redwood will provide a FX reconciliation worksheet as part of the invoice pack.

- Operational note: For any FX adjustment we will require a signed amendment to the Order Form (simple one‑page) to lock in the baseline date and rate source. That keeps a clear audit trail.

Questions for Globex: are you comfortable with a 1.25x cap (we picked below your 1.5x ask) and a quarterly true-up instead of a one-time pass‑through? If you need 1.5x we can escalate for commercial approval but would like to document the ask formally.

Atts: Exhibit-C_Globex_v3_redlines.pdf (legal redline), pricing-scenarios.xlsx (internal notes)

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer | Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Exhibit C markups — commit protection & FX language

Karthik / Rishi — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clearer wording. A couple of responses from Globex legal/finance:

- Cap: 1.25x is acceptable to Globex legal as long as there is a clear reconciliation format and visibility into the monthly usage report before invoicing — that should be added as a schedule to Exhibit C.

- FX: Globex prefers a monthly published rate (we can accept ECB monthly midpoint) and the 3% corridor. However, we are open to Redwood's quarterly true-up if you provide a pro forma monthly FX worksheet for transparency. Jason (cc'd) will own the final reconciliation process on our side.

Next steps from our side: we'll sign the one‑page amendment to lock the baseline if you can (a counter-signed DocuSign link would be best). Also please include the usage report sample as a schedule and the pro forma FX worksheet with the amendment.

I'll route the legal approval once we have the clean redline + amendment + worksheets.

Regards,
Annette
